reason: Measured, the owner-surface half of this is wrong. "Live since 15 July" sits at y=191; the footer's "Updated 15 July 2026" sits at y=1998 in a 2130px document on a 960px viewport (390: 164 vs 1954; 768: 232 vs 2409). That is ~1800px apart, not "eight lines" — the stamp is below the fold on every viewport and is not even present in the owner-flight frame this seat cites (the shot is a 1440x960 viewport clip at 2x). The two strings are never co-visible, sit in different registers (13px vs 11px), and answer different questions, so the claimed "same date twice, so neither reads as load-bearing" rests on a proximity that does not exist. The stamp:false half of the proposed fix is already the artifact's stated rule, applied deliberately with a comment ("No stamp where there is nothing to stamp") on owner-empty, day and ended, and gated ("a project with nothing in it claims no update"); extending it to owner-flight is taste, and it costs the owner the one place they can see the exact line their guests are being shown. The changedAt half is out of scope and cannot pay off. This is a pinned-clock lab (TODAY=2026-07-16, UPDATED=2026-07-15T18:30Z) and fixture.js pins for a stated reason — "a lab that renders a different link on every reload cannot be graded." Wiring changedAt to wall-clock time prints "Updated 24 August 2026" beside a countdown derived from 16 July, the exact self-contradiction the fixture header forbids; wiring it to TODAY buys one digit, once (15 -> 16), at 11px, in a tertiary footer, below the fold, after which it never moves again however many further edits are made — and it buys that in the one surface the same finding wants to delete it from. Adding a mutable changedAt to the fixture record that mirrors the shipped DTOs is data-model work, explicitly out of scope. "Wired to nothing" is also false where it matters: the stamp renders F.updatedAt, a real record field, exactly as "Live since" renders publication.publishedAt; they print the same instant because this fixture's plan was last edited and published at the same moment, which is a property of the data, not a defect in the design. Finally the fix's own undo clause is wrong on its face: an undo restores prior content, and stamping it as an update tells a guest the plan changed when it did not. Verified by driving owner-flight and owner-editing in chromium at 390/768/1440 — rename and move-a-week do propagate to the in-session preview surface, and only the stamp does not, which is the one true grain here; it is a one-character payoff behind a data-model build, not a 9.5-bar improvement.
